_doc: pc/tools/ps1_source_edits.py: the result a void function leaves in $v0. A matched function declared void whose last act on every path is a call keeps that callee's $v0, and a caller that declares it as returning a value reads it on the console. On x86-64 %rax after a void function is whatever it last held (gcc pops a stack argument into %rax on the way out of TmdTG3). Each entry returns the callee's value, for the PC build only (matched sources unedited); audit_ps1_call_args.py reports the shape as VOID-READ. edits: [old, new(, count)] exact replacements, line count kept; a stale entry stops the build.

main/TmdF3.why: TmdF3 is void on the console too, but every path ends in a call to a GsTMD builder and nothing writes $v0 after the jal (retail listing: jal ... lw ra / jr ra), so the builder's packet cursor is TmdF3's result; GsSortObject4 stores it in GsOUT_PACKET_P. ev_final_taco98: gcc's `pop %rax` after the call handed GsSortObject4 the OT header address (ot_work) as the cursor and TACO's GT3 packets overwrote the ordering-table headers.

main/_SpuIsInAllocateArea_.why: void on the console too, but its last act is `jal _SpuIsInAllocateArea` and the epilogue writes no v0, so the callee's 0 / 1 is the result; SpuSetReverb and SpuSetReverbModeParam branch on it (`if (_SpuIsInAllocateArea_(...) != 0)`).  On x86-64 %rax after the void wrapper is not that value.  Found by audit_ps1_call_args.py VOID-READ (2026-11-01: 347 live rows once naked aliases count as returning; this and the TmdXX dispatchers are the ones a branch consumes outside the dead EVENT / GYOZI).
